title: Making The Big Broadcast in Hollywood
summary: The band drove to California and recorded the film sound live on the spot; Black musicians felt an uncomfortable atmosphere in the white world of Hollywood.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: At that time. Were you with Cab when he did that first movie, "Big Broadcast?"
Yes. Yes.
You were with that band?
Yes, I was with that band.
I just saw that movie recently.
Uh-huh.
Now what was that like, do you -- did you pre-record the track?

No, we went to California, I drove all the way out there without stopping, I'll never forget, I'll never get over it, either. Drove to California -- no we didn't do any pre-recording at all. That was done right on the spot.
Uh-huh. With those actors and the --
Oh, yes.
-- the microphone jumping up and down --
Yes.
-- all that nonsense.
Right on the spot.
Nonsense going on.
Uh-huh.
How was a black band treated out in Hollywood, then, I mean you were with all these white actors and it was sort of a white world?

Well, you could tell that there was an atmosphere, of you know, atmosphere wasn't too great for us. They did try to treat us very nice out there. We had no problems at all, but you could always tell, you know, it was something that you didn't feel quite comfortable.
Uh-huh.
You know, you couldn't do just what you wanted to do or go where you wanted to go.
